question.text: An FPI shall transact in the secondary market only on the basis of:

answer.text: Either delivery or cash settlement at the FPI's option
Taking and giving delivery of securities purchased or sold
Cash settlement without any delivery obligation
Net settlement of positions at the end of each trading day

explanation.text: The Logic: In secondary-market investments, an FPI shall transact only on the basis of taking and giving delivery of securities purchased or sold. The Trap: Cash-only or net settlement is not the general rule; delivery is the default for secondary-market FPI transactions, with specific exceptions for derivatives, short-selling, market making, and other transactions specified by the Board. Note: The delivery-based rule and its listed exceptions sit together in the FPI regulations; the exceptions do not displace the underlying requirement for ordinary cash-market trades.
